citations.narrative:
The facility's outdoor primary enclosure for three rabbits did not effectively contain all of the animals.
Employees reported that around mid-May, a 3-4 month old dwarf rabbit ("Trixie") escaped her outdoor enclosure. Due to
her small size, speed, and agility, catching Trixie took a full day and a team of six employees. Employees reported that
after catching her, they subsequently returned her to the outdoor enclosure unharmed. The facility added a high-gauge
mesh fencing to the enclosure to prevent future escapes.
Employees did not realize a small gap remained. Around June 6, Trixie escaped a second time and took residence under
an unused chicken shelter adjacent to her enclosure. Employees reported that this time, there were only two part-time
employees available to attempt to catch Trixie, and efforts were ineffective. Employees set several traps around the area,
checked on her several times daily and provided food and water. Approximately 6 days later, Trixie was successfully
trapped and relocated to an indoor enclosure. Trixie appeared in good health.
The primary enclosure was not maintained in an appropriate condition to effectively contain this rabbit, leading to two
escapes. Escapes can be detrimental to animals' health and well-being.
The facility mended the gap in the enclosure and Trixie is still housed indoors. Continue to correct from this day forward
by ensuring primary enclosures are maintained in good repair to protect the rabbits from injury, to contain them, and to
keep predators out.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
